{y}\n804\t            </span>\n805\t          ))}\n806\t        </div>\n807\t        <ol className=\"timeline__rows\" aria-label=\"Career timeline\">\n808\t          {items.map((item) => {\n809\t 1].year}`,\n    },\n    {\n      id: 'repos',\n      value: github.profile.publicRepos,\n      label: 'Public repositories',\n      hint: `${formatNumber(github.totals.ownRepositories)} original incl. organizations`,\n    },\n    { id: 'gists', value: github.profile.publicGists, label: 'Public gists', hint: 'snippets, notes & logs' },\n    {\n      id: 'packages',\n      value: packages,\n      label: 'Published packages',\n      hint: github.registries.map((r) => r.name).join(' · '),\n    },\n    {\n      id: 'downloads',\n      value: lifetime.reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.downloads, 0),\n      label: 'Package downloads',\n      hint: `lifetime, ${lifetime.map((r) => r.name).join(' + ')}`,\n    },\n    { id: 'stars', value: github.totals.stars, label: 'Stars on own projects', hint: 'personal + organizations' },\n    {\n      id: 'followers',\n      value: github.profile.followers,\n      label: 'GitHub followers',\n      hint: `following ${formatNumber(github.profile.following)}`,\n    },\n    { id: 'years', value: now.getFullYear() - codingSince, label: 'Years of coding', hint: `since ${codingSince}` },\n  ];\n}\n\nexport default function StatTiles({ github, codingSince }) {\n  const stats = buildStats(github, codingSince);\n  return (\n    <ul className=\"stats\" aria-label=\"Key numbers\">\n      {stats.map((s) => (\n        <li key={s.id} className=\"stat\">\n          <span className=\"stat__value\" title={formatNumber(s.value)}>\n            {s.value >= 10000 ? formatCompact(s.value) : formatNumber(s.value)}\n          </span>\n          <span className=\"stat__label\">{s.label}</span>\n          <span className=\"stat__hint\">{s.hint}</span>\n        </li>\n      ))}\n    </ul>\n  );\n}\nimport { Tooltip, useTooltip } from './Tooltip';\n\nconst MONTHS = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];\n\n// 'YYYY-MM' -> fractional year (start of month).\nexport const toYear = (ym) => {\n  const [year, month] = ym.split('-').map(Number);\n  return year + (month - 1) / 12;\n};\n\nexport const formatPeriod = (start, end) => {\n  const fmt = (ym) => {\n    const [year, month] = ym.split('-').map(Number);\n    return `${MONTHS[month - 1]} ${year}`;\n  };\n  return `${fmt(start)} – ${end ? fmt(end) : 'present'}`;\n};\n\nconst TYPES = {\n  company: 'Employment',\n  'open-source': 'Founded / led open-source',\n};\n\nconst linkProps = (url) => (url ? { href: url, target: '_blank', rel: 'noopener noreferrer' } : {});\n\n// Gantt-style overview (one row per position, years on the x axis) followed by\n// position cards, most recent first. Employment and open-source ventures differ\n// by fill style (solid vs. hatched) as well as color, so the distinction never\n// relies on color alone.\nexport default function Timeline({ items, endYear }) {\n  const { tip, show, hide } = useTooltip();\n  const startYear = Math.floor(Math.min(...items.map((i) => toYear(i.start))));\n  const span = endYear + 1 - startYear;\n  const pos = (year) => ((year - startYear) / span) * 100;\n  const ticks = [];\n  for (let y = startYear; y <= endYear; y += 2) ticks.push(y);\n  const recentFirst = [...items].sort(\n    (a, b) => (b.end || '9999').localeCompare(a.end || '9999') || b.start.localeCompare(a.start),\n  );\n\n  const tipContent = (item) => (\n    <>\n      <strong>{item.title}</strong>\n      <span className=\"tooltip__value\">{formatPeriod(item.start, item.end)}</span>\n      <span className=\"tooltip__row\">\n        {item.role} · {TYPES[item.type]}\n      </span>\n    </>\n  );\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"timeline\">\n      <div className=\"chart timeline__chart\" data-tooltip-root>\n        <ul className=\"legend\" aria-label=\"Timeline legend\">\n          {Object.entries(TYPES).map(([type, label]) => (\n            <li key={type}>\n              <span className={`legend__swatch timeline__swatch--${type}`} />\n              {label}\n            </li>\n          ))}\n        </ul>\n        <div className=\"timeline__axis\" aria-hidden=\"true\">\n          {ticks.map((y) => (\n            <span key={y} className=\"timeline__year\" style={{ left: `${pos(y)}%` }}>\n              {y}\n            </span>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n        <ol className=\"timeline__rows\" aria-label=\"Career timeline\">\n          {items.map((item) => {\n            const from = toYear(item.start);\n            const to = item.end ? toYear(item.end) + 1 / 12 : endYear + 1;\n            return (\n              <li key={item.id} className=\"timeline__row\">\n                <span className=\"timeline__label\">{item.title}</span>\n                <span className=\"timeline__track\">\n                  {ticks.map((y) => (\n                    <span key={y} className=\"timeline__tick\" style={{ left: `${pos(y)}%` }} />\n                  ))}\n                  <span\n                    className={`timeline__bar timeline__bar--${item.type}${item.end ? '' : ' is-ongoing'}`}\n                    style={{ left: `${pos(from)}%`, width: `${Math.max(0.8, pos(to) - pos(from))}%` }}\n                    tabIndex={0}\n                    aria-label={`${item.title}, ${item.role}: ${formatPeriod(item.start, item.end)}`}\n                    onPointerMove={(e) => show(e, tipContent(item))}\n                    onFocus={(e) => show(e, tipContent(item))}\n                    onPointerLeave={hide}\n                    onBlur={hide}\n                  />\n                </span>\n              </li>\n            );\n          })}\n        </ol>\n        <Tooltip tip={tip} />\n      </div>\n\n      <ol className=\"positions\">\n        {recentFirst.map((item) => {\n          const Title = item.url ? 'a' : 'span';\n          return (\n            <li key={item.id} className={`position position--${item.type}`}>\n              <span className=\"position__period mono\">{formatPeriod(item.start, item.end)}</span>\n              <h3 className=\"position__title\">\n                <Title {...linkProps(item.url)}>{item.title}</Title>\n              </h3>\n              <span className=\"position__role\">{item.role}</span>\n              <p className=\"position__summary\">{item.summary}</p>\n              <ul className=\"tags\">\n                {item.tags.map((t) => (\n                  <li key={t}>{t}</li>\n                ))}\n              </ul>\n            </li>\n          );\n        })}\n      </ol>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\nimport { useCallback, useState } from 'react';\n\n// Shared hover tooltip: charts call `show(event, content)` on pointer\n// move/focus and `hide()` on leave; the container must be position: relative.\nexport function useTooltip() {\n  const [tip, setTip] = useState(null);\n  const show = useCallback((event, content) => {\n    const box = event.currentTarget.closest('[data-tooltip-root]').getBoundingClientRect();\n    let x;\n    let y;\n    if (event.clientX === undefined || (event.clientX === 0 && event.clientY === 0)) {\n      const target = event.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect();\n      x = target.left + target.width / 2 - box.left;\n      y = target.top - box.top;\n    } else {\n      x = event.clientX - box.left;\n      y = event.clientY - box.top;\n    }\n    setTip({ x, y, content, flip: x > box.width * 0.6 });\n  }, []);\n  const hide = useCallback(() => setTip(null), []);\n  return { tip, show, hide };\n}\n\nexport function Tooltip({ tip }) {\n  if (!tip) return null;\n  return (\n    <div className={`tooltip${tip.flip ? ' tooltip--flip' : ''}`} role=\"status\" style={{ left: tip.x, top: tip.y }}>\n      {tip.content}\n    </div>\n  );\n}\nconst numberFormat = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US');\nconst compactFormat = new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { notation: 'compact', maximumFractionDigits: 1 });\n\nexport const formatNumber = (value) => numberFormat.format(value);\nexport const formatCompact = (value) => compactFormat.format(value);\nexport const formatPercent = (value) => `${(value * 100).toFixed(value < 0.1 ? 1 : 0)}%`;\n\n// Categorical slots validated for the dark surface (#0d1220) with the dataviz\n// palette validator: CVD ΔE ≥ 8.4 on adjacent pairs, contrast ≥ 3:1.\nexport const SERIES = ['#3987e5', '#d95926', '#199e70', '#c98500', '#d55181', '#008300', '#9085e9', '#e66767'];\nimport Existing components and libraries\n\nStar counts and activity come from the GitHub API on 2026-10-16.\n\n### Chart libraries\n\n| Library | Stars | License | Fit for this site |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| [d3/d3](https://github.com/d3/d3) | ~114K | ISC | The most flexible option, but low-level. Its scale and shape helpers would only replace about 20 lines of arithmetic here. |\n| [chartjs/Chart.js](https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js) | ~68K | MIT | Renders to canvas, so marks are not DOM nodes and are harder to make keyboard-accessible or style with CSS. |\n| [apache/echarts](https://github.com/apache/echarts) | ~68K | Apache-2.0 | Very capable, but heavy (hundreds of KB) for 5 small charts. |\n| [recharts/recharts](https://github.com/recharts/recharts) | ~28K | MIT | Good React API for bar and line charts. No Gantt chart or orbit map, and about 100 KB+ gzipped with D3 modules. |\n| [airbnb/visx](https://github.com/airbnb/visx) | ~21K | MIT | Low-level React + D3 primitives. A good choice if the charts grow. |\n| [plouc/nivo](https://github.com/plouc/nivo) | ~14K | MIT | Ready-made calendar, bump and treemap charts. Theming its dark mode to match the site would be about as much work as the hand-written SVG. |\n\n**Decision:** hand-written SVG and CSS. The whole app is **72.6 KB gzipped JS + 5 KB CSS**, every mark is a DOM element that can be styled, focused and tested with Testing Library, and the visual language stays consistent. visx or Recharts would be the natural upgrade path for more complex charts.\n\n### Timelines and activity calendars\n\n| Library | Stars | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| [prabhuignoto/react-chrono](https://github.com/prabhuignoto/react-chrono) | ~4.2K | Vertical, horizontal and tree timelines with cards. It shows sequence but not duration or overlap. Overlap matters here: LinksPlatform runs alongside Abracar and Deep.Foundation. |\n| [stephane-monnot/react-vertical-timeline](https://github.com/stephane-monnot/react-vertical-timeline) | ~1.2K | The classic alternating vertical timeline. It has the same \"list in disguise\" problem. |\n| [grubersjoe/react-activity-calendar](https://github.com/grubersjoe/react-activity-calendar) | ~0.6K | A GitHub-style heatmap. It needs daily data. This site uses yearly totals, because 2025–2026 dominate and a log scale reads better as bars. |\n\n**Decision:** a custom Gantt chart, because overlapping periods are the point of the career story, followed by detail cards.\n\n### Profile and portfolio generators\n\n| Project | Stars | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| [anuraghazra/github-readme-stats](https://github.com/anuraghazra/github-readme-stats) | ~80K | Dynamic SVG cards for READMEs, served from a Vercel API. It covers GitHub only, not companies, registries or publications, and it depends on an external service. |\n| [vn7n24fzkq/github-profile-summary-cards](https://github.com/vn7n24fzkq/github-profile-summary-cards) | ~3.7K | Generates SVG cards in a GitHub Action. Same GitHub-only scope. |\n| [arifszn/gitprofile](https://github.com/arifszn/gitprofile) | ~2.3K | A React portfolio that syncs from a GitHub username. It is the closest match, but fetches GitHub at runtime, is limited to the user's own repositories (not 4 organizations), and has a generic look. |\n| [saadpasta/developerFolio](https://github.com/saadpasta/developerFolio) | ~6.6K | A portfolio template. GPL-3.0, and not actively maintained. |\n| [jsonresume/resume-schema](https://github.com/jsonresume/resume-schema) | ~2.4K | A standard JSON schema for CVs, with many themes. |\n\n**Decision:** none of these is reused directly, but two ideas were adopted:\n\n- the snapshot-based approach of the summary-cards Action (data is generated, not fetched live);\n- a JSON-Resume-like data shape in `src/data/profile.js` (basics, work, education, skills, publications, profiles), which could be exported to `resume.json` later (section 8).\n\n### Visual effects\n\n| Library | Stars | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| [pmndrs/react-three-fiber](https://github.com/pmndrs/react-three-fiber) | ~33K | A 3D background would be very \"futuristic\", but costs more than 150 KB and battery life on phones. |\n| [tsparticles/tsparticles](https://github.com/tsparticles/tsparticles) | ~9K | Particle backgrounds, about 30 KB+. |\n\n**Decision:** CSS gradients, an animated grid and a conic ring give the same look for 0 KB of JS.\n\n## 7. CI and deploy root causes\n\nOn `main`, GitHub Pages had never deployed anything. The original workflow (`.github/workflows/github-pages.yml` as of `main` commit `117f247`) had four independent defects:\n\n1. **Invalid YAML.** The step name `Deploy: Copy build to docs folder and commit` contains an unquoted `: `, so GitHub rejected the file. Run [38958801553](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/38958801553) failed with \"This run likely failed because of a workflow file issue\" (log in [`ci-logs/`](../../../ci-logs)). Fix: quote the name. `src/workflow.test.js` now parses every workflow with js-yaml.\n2. **Nonexistent dependency.** `package.json` had `\"overrides\": {\"@testing-library/react\": \"^19.0.0\"}`, but that package has no version 19 (the latest is 16.x), so `npm ci` and `npm install` could not resolve it. Existing components and libraries\n\nStar counts and activity come from the GitHub API on 2026-10-16.\n\n### Chart libraries\n\n| Library | Stars | License | Fit for this site |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| [d3/d3](https://github.com/d3/d3) | ~114K | ISC | The most flexible option, but low-level. It follows the references in the issue, their original discussions and code, relevant public work in [LinksPlatform][linksplatform] and [Deep Foundation][deep-foundation], and the experiments preserved here. Sources were checked on **2026-10-11**.\n\nThis is an inventory of identified public attempts, open to additions as earlier material is recovered. Dates identify a public comment, commit, or archived artifact, as specified below; they do not automatically establish a project's invention or release date. A source or demo link records evidence, not a guarantee that an old demo still runs in a current browser.\n\n## What the visual needs to express\n\nIn the [links theory][theory-doublets], a doublet-link has a reference of its own and two references to links, conventionally source and target. For example:\n\n```text\n1: (1, 1)   a link whose source and target both refer to itself\n2: (2, 2)   another such link\n3: (1, 2)   a link between those two links\n4: (3, 2)   a link starting from link 3 and ending at link 2\n5: (3, 4)   a link between two links that themselves connect links\n```\n\nThe theory's [network illustrations][theory-figures] depict self-reference using a closed arrow resembling an infinity symbol. The practical visual goal is to make a link's identity and its source/target references readable, including when a reference names another connecting link. Recursive structure and self-reference also need to remain understandable during interaction.\n\nSeveral approaches below use ordinary graph nodes as proxies for links. Those encodings can preserve the references and support useful tools. Whether the picture shows a connection to the actual curve, to a proxy node, or only to a nested textual representation is a separate question. The descriptions distinguish these choices rather than treating every graph view as the same result.\n\n## Timeline\n\n| Date or period | Attempt and evidence | Contribution and remaining boundary |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| 2015-09-16 archive; one page stamped 2011-05-11 | LinksPlatform [Web UI prototypes 1 and 2][web-ui-original] | Hyperlinked descriptions and nested trees expose link structure. The HTML mirror timestamp is evidence of an older artifact, not a verified launch date. |\n| 2015-11-12 | LinksPlatform [doublet][doublet-symbol] and [triplet][triplet-symbol] SVG symbols | Nested circles explore how one link can contain references; these are symbols rather than an editor for a network. |\n| 2016-01-10–14 | Konard's [Cytoscape.js request #1217][cytoscape-request] and the [maintainer's decision][cytoscape-decision] | An edge whose endpoints name edges did not display. Native support was declined because it conflicted with Cytoscape's graph model and algorithms; intermediary and compound nodes were suggested. |\n| 2016-01-12 |\nShell cwd was reset to /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1792426716947",

[Prototype 1][web-ui-1] presents source/linker/target descriptions as hyperlinks and lists referring links. Its HTML says it was mirrored on 2011-05-11. The [2020 circles-ring page][circles-ring-source] generalizes that construction interactively. D3 animates Bézier interpolation and lets the user drag the controls. Its [introduction commit][closed-link-commit] explicitly identifies self-reference as the purpose. This makes the geometry of a self-referencing link visible, but has no collection of link IDs or attachments between multiple curves.\n\n### The Cytoscape request and the two workarounds\n\nOn 2016-01-10, [Konard asked Cytoscape.js][cytoscape-request] to display an edge whose source and target were the IDs of two other edges. The request also included sketches of node-to-edge, edge-to-edge, and recursively encapsulated structures. Konard [clarified][cytoscape-clarification] that the intended relation was binary, with links as both endpoints, rather than an arbitrary-arity hyperedge.\n\nOn January 13, [Max Franz declined native support][cytoscape-decision] after discussing it with the team: Cytoscape's traversal and other algorithms depended on its node/edge model. He suggested application-level nodes or an extension; [the next reply][cytoscape-alternatives] explained intermediary and compound nodes. This records a library design decision, rather than establishing a prohibition on every possible mathematical or visual model.\n\nKonard [posted two implemented examples on January 15][cytoscape-demos-comment], also preserved in the [introduction commit][cytoscape-demos-commit]:\n\n| Example | Mechanism in the source | What it demonstrates |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| [Intermediary nodes][intermediary-source] · [demo][intermediary-demo] | Holding a node adds source and target nodes with edges `source → node → target`; holding again removes its generated descendants. | A link can be represented by a node and two reference edges, with repeated expansion. The link is visually split into graph elements. |\n| [Compound nodes][compound-source] · [demo][compound-demo] | Holding a node creates two child nodes and an edge inside that parent; holding again removes the children. | Recursive containment can be explored, while connections still have graph nodes as endpoints. |\n\nBoth handlers rerun the Dagre layout. They establish working responses to the suggestion, with different visual tradeoffs from attaching a connector to an intact link curve.\n\n### Later viewers and explanatory material\n\nThe [RawDoubletsViewer alpha commit][raw-viewer-commit] dates to July 19, 2020. Its [Win32 list-view code][raw-viewer-source] displays stored records, including source and target fields. It supplies direct inspection of doublets, rather than a geometric renderer of connections between them.\n\n[InfiniteDepthTreeWebUIPrototype][tree-prototype] was [moved out of Documentation on July 20, 2020][tree-extraction]. Its README describes viewing and editing deep graphs through a tree, including structures with self-references. [react-deep-tree][react-tree] explicitly identifies that prototype as its starting point and provides a React component for navigating nested content. The tree representation is useful for browsing; it is a different view from depicting shared identity and connections between curves on one canvas.\n\nThe [September 2021 stack drawings][stack-commit] preserve SVG, raster, and editable artwork under [Documentation's visualization archive][visualizations-archive]. The [November introduction animation draft][intro-animation-commit] adds an SVG animation and an HTML wrapper. These are explanatory visual artifacts; neither commit establishes a general interactive links editor.\n\n## GoJS: an early implementation using link label nodes\n\n# Case Study: Issue #28 - Make grid mode closer to single-link mode\n\n## Overview\n\n**Issue:** [#28 - We need to make sure multi link (grid) mode is closer to single link mode](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/issues/28)\n\n**Pull request:** [#29](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals/pull/29)\n\n**Affected page:** `grid.html`\n\n**Reference pages that must be preserved:** `blueprint.html`, `animated-blueprint.html`\n\n## Archived Evidence\n\n- Raw issue data: [`raw/issue.json`](./raw/issue.json)\n- Raw issue comments: [`raw/issue-comments.json`](./raw/issue-comments.json)\n- Raw PR data/comments/reviews: [`raw/pr.json`](./raw/pr.json), [`raw/pr-conversation-comments.json`](./raw/pr-conversation-comments.json), [`raw/pr-review-comments.json`](./raw/pr-review-comments.json), [`raw/pr-reviews.json`](./raw/pr-reviews.json)\n- Related issue/PR data: [`raw/related-issue-23.json`](./raw/related-issue-23.json), [`raw/related-pr-24.json`](./raw/related-pr-24.json), [`raw/related-pr-25.json`](./raw/related-pr-25.json), [`raw/related-pr-26.json`](./raw/related-pr-26.json)\n- Issue screenshot: [`images/grid-mess-layout.png`](./images/grid-mess-layout.png)\n- After screenshot: [`images/grid-after.png`](./images/grid-after.png)\n- Reproduction log: [`raw/grid-e2e-before.log`](./raw/grid-e2e-before.log)\n- Verification logs: [`raw/grid-e2e-after.log`](./raw/grid-e2e-after.log), [`raw/unit-after.log`](./raw/unit-after.log), [`raw/e2e-after.log`](./raw/e2e-after.log)\n\n## Timeline\n\n1. **March 17, 2026:** Issue #23 requested a grid page based on the best practices from `blueprint.html`. It specified a square grid, fixed link centers, self-referencing default links, one slider for link count, localStorage persistence, and a reset button.\n2. **March 17, 2026:** PRs #24, #25, and #26 iterated on `grid.html`. They added a colored multi-link grid, then revised control point style and fixed centers to match issue #23 comments.\n3. **June 21, 2026:** Issue #28 reported that grid mode still diverged too much from single-link mode, especially in control point/arrow proportions and layout reset behavior.\n4. **June 25, 2026:** This investigation archived issue/PR data, reproduced the failures with a new grid E2E test, fixed the grid rendering model, and verified the full test suite.\n5. **June 25, 2026:** PR review feedback (\"Control points color cannot be changed, or proportions must be preserved\") flagged that grid control points were tinted with the per-link color and drawn with a 2px stroke. Fixed by restoring blueprint's fixed semantic colors (green/red/black/blue), 1px dashed outline, and the missing blue intermediate control points.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. Keep `blueprint.html` and `animated-blueprint.html` unchanged.\n2. Make grid links look like the single-link blueprint, with color as the only visual override. The per-link color applies to the link itself (path + endpoint markers) only; control point colors are fixed and must never change.\n3. Preserve blueprint proportions for path strokes, endpoint markers, control point radii, snap threshold, IK segment length, and offsets.\n4. Keep grid link centers fixed in a square grid.\n5. Keep default links self-referencing, with start and end at the fixed center.\n6. Preserve localStorage layout persistence.\n7. Add a layout reset that actually restores default positions.\n8. Archive issue data, related history, screenshots, logs, and analysis in `docs/case-studies/issue-28`.\n9. Add tests that fail before the fix and pass after it.\n\n## Root Causes\n\n### 1. Mixed Scale Model\n\nBefore the fix, `grid.html` used one value for arrangement (`gridUnit`) and another for link geometry (`segLen = gridUnit * 0.35`). Control point radius used `gridUnit`, while path stroke and markers used `segLen`.\n\nAt a 1200 by 800 viewport with 4 links, the failing reproduction captured:\n\n- Expected control radius from blueprint-style local spacing: `4.56`\n- Actual control radius before fix: `25.84`\n\nThat made control circles much larger than the link geometry and made marker proportions diverge from the reference pages.\n\n### 2. Reset Reused Dirty Link State\n\nThe reset button cleared localStorage and reset the link count, but `initLinks()` still preserved `oldLinks` when saved data was absent. After moving a link endpoint and clicking reset, the moved endpoint survived.\n\nThe failing reproduction captured:\n\n- Expected `cp-end-0` x after reset: `448`\n- Actual `cp-end-0` x after reset: `524`\n\n### 3. Absolute Position Persistence\n\nSaved layouts used absolute `{ x, y }` coordinates. That differs from the blueprint model, where point positions are represented as factors of `gridSpacing`. Absolute values make saved layouts less responsive to viewport and grid-size changes.\n\n### 4. Control Points Tinted With the Link Color\n\nGrid control points were drawn with colors derived from the per-link color: start blended the link color with green, end blended it with red, and center used the raw link color, all with a 2px stroke. The blue IK-controlled intermediate control points from blueprint.html were missing entirely.\n\nThis contradicted the core requirement that \"the only change that can be applied at multi line link is color\" — meaning only the link (path + markers) is recolored, while control points must keep their fixed semantic meaning. In `blueprint.html` / `js/control-points.mjs` those colors are fixed: start = green, end = red, center = black, intermediate = blue, with a 1px dashed (`4 2`) outline. The grid therefore looked different from single mode even though both render the same geometry.\n\n## Solution\n\n1. Added `js/blueprint-link.mjs` as a small reusable helper for grid mode:\n   - `createBlueprintMetrics(gridSpacing)`\n   - `computeBlueprintLinkPoints(link, metrics)`\nShell cwd was reset to /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1792426716947",

Control Points Tinted With the Link Color\n\nGrid control points were drawn with colors derived from the per-link color: start blended the link color with green, end blended it with red, and center used the raw link color, all with a 2px stroke. The blue IK-controlled intermediate control points from blueprint.html were missing entirely.\n\nThis contradicted the core requirement that \"the only change that can be applied at multi line link is color\" — meaning only the link (path + markers) is recolored, while control points must keep their fixed semantic meaning. In `blueprint.html` / `js/control-points.mjs` those colors are fixed: start = green, end = red, center = black, intermediate = blue, with a 1px dashed (`4 2`) outline. The grid therefore looked different from single mode even though both render the same geometry.\n\n## Solution\n\n1. Added `js/blueprint-link.mjs` as a small reusable helper for grid mode:\n   - `createBlueprintMetrics(gridSpacing)`\n   - `computeBlueprintLinkPoints(link, metrics)`",

Promise.resolve()\n  let release\n  const current = new Promise((resolve) => (release = resolve))\n  hostQueue.set(host, previous.then(() => current))\n  await previous\n  setTimeout(release, gap)\n}\n\nasync function request(url, { method = 'GET', headers = {}, body, as = 'json', tries = 5, timeout = 60000 } = {}) {\n  const host = new URL(url).host\n  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {\n    await throttle(host)\n    try {\n      const res = await fetch(url, { method, body, headers: { 'User-Agent': UA, Accept: as === 'json' ? 'application/json' : '*/*', ...headers }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeout), redirect: 'follow' })\n      if ((res.status === 429 || res.status >= 500) && attempt < tries) {\n        const retryAfter = Number(res.headers.get('retry-after')) || 0\n        await res.arrayBuffer().catch(() => {})\n        await sleep(Math.min(60000, Math.max(retryAfter * 1000, 2000 * 2 ** (attempt - 1))))\n        continue\n      }\n      const text = await res.text()\n      let data = text\n      if (as === 'json') {\n        try { data = JSON.parse(text) } catch { data = null }\n      }\n      return { status: res.status, ok: res.ok, data }\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (attempt >= tries) return { status: 0, ok: false, data: null, error: String(error.message || error) }\n      await sleep(2000 * attempt)\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nasync function pool(items, size, fn) {\n  const results = new Array(items.length)\n  let next = 0\n  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(size, items.length) }, async () => {\n    while (next < items.length) {\n      const i = next++\n      results[i] = await fn(items[i], i)\n    }\n  }))\n  return results\n}\n\nfunction gh(args) {\n  return new Promise((resolve) => {\n    execFile('gh', args, { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 1 << 28 }, (error, stdout, stderr) => {\n      if (error) return resolve({ ok: false, error: (stderr || error.message || '').trim().split('\\n')[0] })\n      try { resolve({ ok: true, data: JSON.parse(stdout) }) } catch { resolve({ ok: true, data: stdout }) }\n    })\n  })\n}\nasync function ghRetry(args, tries = 3) {\n  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {\n    const result = await gh(args)\n    if (result.ok || attempt >= tries || /404|409|Not Found|empty/i.test(result.error)) return result\n    await sleep(3000 * attempt)\n  }\n}\n\n// ------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers\nconst repos = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(REPOS_FILE, 'utf8'))\nconst OWNERS = [...new Set(repos.map((r) => r.owner))]\nconst escapeRe = (s) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&')\nconst OWNER_RE = new RegExp(`(?:github\\\\.com[/:](${OWNERS.map(escapeRe).join('|')})(?:/|$)|(?:^|/)(${OWNERS.map(escapeRe).join('|')})\\\\.github\\\\.io)`, 'i')\nconst pointsToOwners = (...urls) => urls.flat().filter((u) => typeof u === 'string').some((u) => OWNER_RE.test(u))\nconst repoUrl = (value) => (typeof value === 'string' ? value : value && value.url) || null\nconst cleanRepo = (u) => (u ? String(s).replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, n) : null)\nconst sum = (list, key = 'downloads') => list.reduce((a, p) => a + (Number(p[key]) || 0), 0)\n\nfunction registry(id, name, url, extra = {}) {\n  return { id, name, url, accounts: [], packages: [], discovery: [], status: 'none', note: null, ...extra }\n}\nfunction finish(reg, { downloadsPeriod } = {}) {\n  reg.packages.sort((a, b) => (b.downloads || 0) - (a.downloads || 0) || a.name.localeCompare(b.name))\n  reg.totals = { packages: reg.packages.length, downloads: sum(reg.packages) }\n  if (downloadsPeriod !== undefined) reg.totals.downloadsPeriod = downloadsPeriod\n  if (reg.packages.length) reg.status = reg.status === 'blocked' ? 'partial' : 'ok'\n  return reg\n}\nasync function guarded(id, fn) {\n  try {\n    log(`start ${id}`)\n    const reg = await fn()\n    log(`done  ${id}: ${reg.status}, ${reg.packages.length} packages`)\n    return reg\n  } catch (error) {\n    log(`FAIL  ${id}: ${error.stack || error}`)\n    return { id, name: id, status: 'blocked', note: `collector error: ${error.message}`, accounts: [], MAX_PER_KIND = 60\n\nasync function discoverManifests() {\n  const candidates = { npm: [], crates: [], pypi: [], rubygems: [], packagist: [], pub: [], hex: [], go: [], nuget: [], swift: [], maven: [], }\n    if (res.data.truncated) truncated++\n    const files = res.data.tree.filter((t) => t.type === 'blob').map((t) => t.path)\n    const counts = {}\n    for (const file of files) {\n      if (/^homebrew-/i.test(repo.name) && /^(Formula|Casks?)\\/.+\\.rb$/.test(file)) {\n        candidates.homebrew.push({ repo: repo.fullName, path: file, name: path.basename(file, '.rb'), kind: rawCache = new Map()\nasync function raw(repo, file) {\n  const key = `${repo}/${file}`\n  if (!rawCache.has(key)) {\n    rawCache.set(key, function manifestNames(list, parse) {\n  const out = new Map()\n  await pool(list, 8, async (c) => {\n    const text = await raw(c.repo, c.path)\n    if (!text) return\n    let names\n    try { names [...String(res.data).matchAll(/<string>([^<]*)<\\/string>\\s*<\\/value>\\s*<value><string>([^<]*)<\\/string>/g)].map((m) => [m[1], m[2]]) : []\n    reg.accounts.push({ account, kind: 'user', url: `https://pypi.org/user/${account}/`, found: pairs.length > 0, packages: pairs.length, ...(res.ok ? Object.values(info.project_urls || {}) : []\n    reg.packages.push({\n      name,\n      version: info ? info.version : null,\n      description: short(info && info.summary),\n      url: `https://pypi.org/project/${name}/`,\n      repository: urls.find((u) => /github\\.com/.test(u)) || (info && info.home_page) || null,\n      downloads: stats.ok && stats.data ? stats.data.data.last_month : null,\n      downloadsPeriod: 'last-month',\n      lastWeek: stats.ok && stats.data ? stats.data.data.last_week : null,\n      sources: roles.get(name),\n    })\n  }\n  reg.note = 'Downloads from pypistats.org (last 30 days, excludes mirrors).'\n  return finish(reg, { downloadsPeriod: 'last-month' })\n}\n\n// =========================================================== Docker Hub\nasync function collectDocker() {\n  const reg = registry('dockerhub', 'Docker Hub', `https://hub.docker.com/u/${USER}`)\n  for (const ns of DOCKER_NAMESPACES) {\n    const [u, o] = [await request(`https://hub.docker.com/v2/users/${ns}/`), await request(`https://hub.docker.com/v2/orgs/${ns}/`)]\n    const exists = u.ok || o.ok\n    let count = 0\n    if (exists) {\n      let url = `https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/${ns}/?page_size=100`\n      while (url) {\n        const res = await request(url)\n        if (!res.ok) break\n        for (const r of res.data.results) {\n          count++\n          reg.packages.push({\n            name: `${r.namespace}/${r.name}`,\n            version: null,\n            description: short(r.description),\n            url: `https://hub.docker.com/r/${r.namespace}/${r.name}`,\n            downloads: r.pull_count,\n            downloadsPeriod: 'all-time pulls',\n            stars: r.star_count,\n            lastUpdated: r.last_updated,\n          })\n        }\n        url = res.data.next\n      }\n    }\n    reg.accounts.push({ account: ns, kind: u.ok ? 'user' : o.ok ? 'org' : null, url: `https://hub.docker.com/u/${ns}`, found: exists, packages: count })\n  }\n  reg.note = 'downloads = all-time pull_count.'\n  return finish(reg, { downloadsPeriod: 'all-time pulls' })\n}\n\n// ============================================ GitHub Packages (ghcr.io etc.)\nconst parseCount = (s) => {\n  const m = String(s).trim().match(/^([\\d.,]+)\\s*([kKmMbB])?$/)\n  if (!m) return null\n  const n = parseFloat(m[1].replace(/,/g, ''))\n  return Math.round(n * ({ k: 1e3, m: 1e6, b: 1e9 }[(m[2] || '').toLowerCase()] || 1))\n}\nasync function collectGithubPackages() {\n  const reg = registry('github-packages', 'GitHub Packages (ghcr.io, npm.pkg.github.com, ...)', `https://github.com/${USER}?tab=packages`)\n  const api = await gh(['api', `users/${USER}/packages?package_type=container&per_page=1`])\n  const apiBlocked = !api.ok\n  reg.discovery.push(apiBlocked ? `REST API blocked: ${api.error} - fell back to public HTML package pages` : 'REST API available')\n  const owners = [[USER, 'user'], ...OWNERS.filter((o) => o !== USER).map((o) => [o, 'org'])]\n  for (const [owner, kind] of owners) {\n    let count = 0\n    let exists = false\n    for (let page = 1; page <= 50; page++) {\n      const url = kind === 'user' ? `https://github.com/${owner}?tab=packages&page=${page}` : `https://github.com/orgs/${owner}/packages?page=${page}`\n      const res = await request(url, { as: 'text' })\n      if (!res.ok) break\n      exists = true\n      const html = String(res.data)\n      const rows = html.split('<li class=\"Box-row\">').slice(1)\n      let added = 0\n      for (const row of rows) {\n        const link = row.match(/href=\"(\\/(?:orgs|users)\\/[^/]+\\/packages\\/([^/]+)\\/package\\/([^\"]+))\"/)\n        if (!link) continue\n        const name = decodeURIComponent(link[3])\n        const published = row.match(/<relative-time datetime=\"([^\"]+)\"/)\n        const repo = row.match(/in <strong><a [^>]*href=\"\\/([^\"]+)\"/)\n        const dl = row.match(/octicon-download[\\s\\S]*?<\\/svg>\\s*([^<\\s][^<]*?)\\s*<\\/span>/)\n        reg.packages.push({\n          name: `${owner}/${name}`,\n          type: link[2],\n          version: null,\n          description: null,\n          url: `https://github.com${link[1]}`,\n          repository: repo ? `https://github.com/${repo[1]}` : null,\n          publishedAt: published ? published[1] : null,\n          downloads: dl ? parseCount(dl[1]) : null,\n          downloadsText: dl ? dl[1].trim() : null,\n          downloadsPeriod: 'all-time (rounded, as shown on github.com)',\n        })\n        added++\n      }\n      count += added\n      if (!added || !new RegExp(`[?&]page=${page + 1}\\\\b`).test(html)) break\n    }\n    reg.accounts.push({ account: owner, kind, url: kind === 'user' ? `https://github.com/${owner}?tab=packages` : `https://github.com/orgs/${owner}/packages`, found: exists, packages: count })\n  }\n  if (apiBlocked) {\n    reg.status = 'blocked'\n    reg.blocker = 'gh token lacks read:packages scope; exact download counts and versions need `gh auth refresh -s read:packages`.'\n  }\n  reg.note = 'Scraped from public github.com package listings; download counts are rounded by GitHub (e.g. 1.37k). Only public packages are visible.'\n  return finish(reg, { downloadsPeriod: 'all-time (rounded)' })\n}\n\n// ================================================================= RubyGems\nasync function collectRubygems(manifest) {\n  const reg = registry('rubygems', 'RubyGems', `https://rubygems.org/profiles/${USER}`)\n  const found = new Map()\n  const toPkg = (g, source) => ({ name: g.name, version: g.version, description: short(g.info), url: g.project_uri, repository: g.source_code_uri || g.homepage_uri, downloads: g.downloads, downloadsPeriod: 'all-time', sources: [source] })\n  for (const account of NAMES) {\n    const res = await request(`https://rubygems.org/api/v1/owners/${account}/gems.json`)\n    const list = res.ok && Array.isArray(res.data) ? res.data : []\n    reg.accounts.push({ account, kind: 'owner', url: `https://rubygems.org/profiles/${account}`, found: res.ok, packages: list.length, ...(res.ok ? {} : { httpStatus: res.status }) })\n    for (const g of list) found.set(g.name, toPkg(g, `owner:${account}`))\n  }\n  const names = await manifestNames(manifest.rubygems, (text) => {\n    const m = text.match(/\\.name\\s*=\\s*[\"']([^\"']+)[\"']/)\n    return m && m[1]\n  })\n  let hits = 0\n  await pool(names.filter((n) => !found.has(n.name)), 6, async (n) => {\n    const res = await request(`https://rubygems.org/api/v1/gems/${encodeURIComponent(n.name)}.json`)\n    if (res.ok && res.data && pointsToOwners(res.data.source_code_uri, res.data.homepage_uri, res.data.bug_tracker_uri)) {\n      found.set(res.data.name, toPkg(res.data, `manifest:${n.repo}`))\n      hits++\n    }\n  })\n  reg.discovery.push(`${names.length} gemspec names in repos, ${hits} confirmed`)\n  reg.packages = [...found.values()]\n  return finish(reg, { downloadsPeriod: 'all-time' })\n}\n\n// ================================================================= Packagist\nasync function collectPackagist(manifest) {\n  const reg = registry('packagist', 'Packagist (PHP)', `https://packagist.org/users/${USER}/`)\n  const names = new Map()\n  for (const vendor of [...new Set([...NAMES, ...OWNERS.map((o) => o.toLowerCase())])]) {\n    const res = await request(`https://packagist.org/packages/list.json?vendor=${vendor}`)\n    const list = res.ok && res.data ? res.data.packageNames : []\n    reg.accounts.push({ account: vendor, kind: 'vendor', url: `https://packagist.org/packages/${vendor}/`, found: list.length > 0, packages: list.length })\n    for (const n of list) names.set(n, `vendor:${vendor}`)\n  }\n  const fromRepos = await manifestNames(manifest.packagist, (text) => JSON.parse(text).name)\n  for (const n of fromRepos) if (!names.has(n.name)) names.set(n.name, `manifest:${n.repo}`)\n  for (const [name, source] of names) {\n    const res = await request(`https://packagist.org/packages/${name}.json`)\n    if (!res.ok || !res.data || !res.data.package) continue\n    const p = res.data.package\n    if (source.startsWith('manifest:') && !pointsToOwners(p.repository)) continue\n    reg.packages.push({ name, version: null, description: short(p.description), url: `https://packagist.org/packages/${name}`, repository: p.repository, downloads: p.downloads.total, downloadsPeriod: 'all-time', monthly: p.downloads.monthly, sources: [source] })\n  }\n  reg.discovery.push(`vendor listings; ${fromRepos.length} composer.json names in repos checked`)\n  return finish(reg, { downloadsPeriod: 'all-time' })\n}\n\n// ======================================================= Go module proxy\nconst goEscape = (p) => p.replace(/[A-Z]/g, (c) => `!${c.toLowerCase()}`)\nasync function collectGo(manifest) {\n  const reg = registry('go', 'Go module proxy (proxy.golang.org / pkg.go.dev)', 'https://pkg.go.dev/')\n  const modules = await manifestNames(manifest.go, (text) => {\n    const m = text.match(/^module\\s+(\\S+)/m)\n    return m && m[1].replace(/[\"']/g, '')\n  })\n  for (const mod of modules) {\n    if (!pointsToOwners(`https://${mod}/`)) {\n      reg.discovery.push(`skipped ${mod} (${mod.startsWith('github.com/') ? 'foreign owner' : 'not a github.com path'}, from ${mod.repo || 'repo'})`)\n      continue\n    }\n    const list = await request(`https://proxy.golang.org/${goEscape(mod.name)}/@v/list`, { as: 'text' })\n    const latest = await request(`https://proxy.golang.org/${goEscape(mod.name)}/@latest`)\n    if (!latest.ok) continue\n    const tags = list.ok ? String(list.data).split('\\n').filter(Boolean) : []\n    reg.packages.push({\n      name: mod.name,\n      version: latest.data.Version,\n      description: null,\n      url: `https://pkg.go.dev/${mod.name}`,\n      repository: `https://github.com/${mod.repo}`,\n      taggedVersions: tags.length,\n      pseudoVersionOnly: tags.length === 0,\n      publishedAt: latest.data.Time,\n      downloads: null,\n      downloadsPeriod: 'not published by the Go proxy',\n    })\n  }\n  reg.accounts.push({ account: 'go.mod files in all repositories', kind: 'derived', found: modules.length > 0, packages: modules.length })\n  reg.discovery.push(`${modules.length} go.mod module paths found in repos`)\n  reg.note = 'The Go proxy serves any public module on demand; pseudoVersionOnly=true means no semver tag was ever published. Go has no public download counts.'\n  return finish(reg, { downloadsPeriod: null })\n}\n\n// ===================================================================== JSR\nasync function collectJsr() {\n  const reg = registry('jsr', 'JSR', 'https://jsr.io/')\n  for (const scope of [...new Set([...NAMES, 'deepcase', 'linksplatform'])]) {\n    const res = await request(`https://api.jsr.io/scopes/${scope}/packages?limit=100`)\n    const items = res.ok && res.data ? res.data.items || [] : []\n    reg.accounts.push({ account: `@${scope}`, kind: 'scope', url: `https://jsr.io/@${scope}`, found: res.ok, packages: items.length, ...(res.ok ? {} : { httpStatus: res.status }) })\n    for (const p of items) reg.packages.push({ name: `@${p.scope}/${p.name}`, version: p.latestVersion, description: short(p.description), url: `https://jsr.io/@${p.scope}/${p.name}`, downloads: null, downloadsPeriod: null })\n  }\n  return finish(reg)\n}\n\n// ================================================== VS Code Marketplace / Open VSX\nasync function collectVscode() {\n  const reg = registry('vscode', 'Visual Studio Marketplace', 'https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/')\n  for (const publisher of NAMES) {\n    const body = JSON.stringify({ filters: [{ criteria: [{ filterType: 18, value: publisher }, { filterType: 8, value: 'Microsoft.VisualStudio.Code' }], pageSize: 100 }], flags: 0x100 | 0x200 | 0x2 })\n    const res = await request('https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/_apis/public/gallery/extensionquery', { method: 'POST', body, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Accept: 'application/json;api-version=7.2-preview.1' } })\n    const exts = res.ok && res.data ? res.data.results[0].extensions.filter((e) => e.publisher.publisherName.toLowerCase() === publisher.toLowerCase()) : []\n    reg.accounts.push({ account: publisher, kind: 'publisher', url: `https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/publishers/${publisher}`, found: exts.length > 0, packages: exts.length })\n    for (const e of exts) {\n      const installs = (e.statistics || []).find((s) => s.statisticName === 'install')\n      reg.packages.push({ name: `${e.publisher.publisherName}.${e.extensionName}`, version: e.versions && e.versions[0] && e.versions[0].version, description: short(e.shortDescription), url: `https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=${e.publisher.publisherName}.${e.extensionName}`, downloads: installs ? installs.value : null, downloadsPeriod: 'all-time installs' })\n    }\n  }\n  return finish(reg)\n}\nasync function collectOpenVsx() {\n  const reg = registry('openvsx', 'Open VSX', 'https://open-vsx.org/')\n  for (const ns of NAMES) {\n    const res = await request(`https://open-vsx.org/api/${ns}`)\n    const exts = res.ok && res.data && res.data.extensions ? Object.keys(res.data.extensions) : []\n    reg.accounts.push({ account: ns, kind: 'namespace', url: `https://open-vsx.org/namespace/${ns}`, found: res.ok, packages: exts.length })\n    for (const name of exts) {\n      const d = (await request(`https://open-vsx.org/api/${ns}/${name}`)).data || {}\n      reg.packages.push({ name: `${ns}.${name}`, version: d.version, description: short(d.description), url: `https://open-vsx.org/extension/${ns}/${name}`, downloads: d.downloadCount, downloadsPeriod: 'all-time' })\n    }\n  }\n  return finish(reg)\n}\n\n// ============================================================ Maven Central\nasync function collectMaven(manifest) {\n  const reg = registry('maven', 'Maven Central', 'https://central.sonatype.com/')\n  const groups = [...new Set(OWNERS.flatMap((o) => [`io.github.${o.toLowerCase()}`, `com.github.${o.toLowerCase()}`]).concat(['com.linksplatform', 'org.linksplatform', 'io.deep-foundation', 'foundation.link']))]\n  for (const g of groups) {\n    const res = await request(`https://search.maven.org/solrsearch/select?q=g:${encodeURIComponent(`\"${g}\"`)}&rows=100&wt=json`)\n    const docs = res.ok && res.data ? res.data.response.docs : []\n    if (docs.length || g.includes(USER)) reg.accounts.push({ account: g, kind: 'groupId', found: docs.length > 0, packages: docs.length, ...(res.ok ? {} : { httpStatus: res.status }) })\n    for (const d of docs) reg.packages.push({ name: `${d.g}:${d.a}`, version: d.latestVersion, description: null, url: `https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/${d.g}/${d.a}`, downloads: null, downloadsPeriod: null, versions: d.versionCount })\n  }\n  reg.discovery.push(`${groups.length} candidate groupIds queried (only konard-related ones and hits are listed in accounts); ${manifest.maven.length} pom.xml/build.gradle files exist in repos`)\n  reg.note = 'Maven Central publishes no per-artifact download counts.'\n  return finish(reg)\n}\n\n// ============================================================ pub.dev / Hex\nasync function collectPub(manifest) {\n  const reg = registry('pub', 'pub.dev (Dart/Flutter)', 'https://pub.dev/')\n  const names = await manifestNames(manifest.pub, (text) => {\n    if (/^publish_to:\\s*['\"]?none/m.test(text)) return null\n    const m = text.match(/^name:\\s*([A-Za-z0-9_]+)/m)\n    return m && m[1]\n  })\n  for (const n of names) {\n    const res = await request(`https://pub.dev/api/packages/${n.name}`)\n    if (!res.ok || !res.data) continue\n    const ps = res.data.latest.pubspec\n    if (!pointsToOwners(ps.repository, ps.homepage, ps.issue_tracker)) continue\n    const score = (await request(`https://pub.dev/api/packages/${n.name}/score`)).data || {}\n    reg.packages.push({ name: n.name, version: res.data.latest.version, description: short(ps.description), url: `https://pub.dev/packages/${n.name}`, repository: ps.repository || ps.homepage, downloads: score.downloadCount30Days ?? null, downloadsPeriod: 'last-30-days' })\n  }\n  reg.accounts.push({ account: 'pubspec.yaml files in all repositories', kind: 'derived', found: names.length > 0, packages: names.length })\n  return finish(reg, { downloadsPeriod: 'last-30-days' })\n}\nasync function collectHex(manifest) {\n  const reg = registry('hex', 'Hex (Elixir/Erlang)', 'https://hex.pm/')\n  for (const account of NAMES) {\n    const res = await request(`https://hex.pm/api/users/${account}`)\n    const pkgs = res.ok && res.data ? res.data.packages || [] : []\n    reg.accounts.push({ account, kind: 'user', url: `https://hex.pm/users/${account}`, found: res.ok, packages: pkgs.length })\n    for (const p of pkgs) reg.packages.push({ name: p.name, url: p.html_url, downloads: null, downloadsPeriod: null })\n  }\n  const names = await manifestNames(manifest.hex, (text) => {\n    const m = text.match(/\\bapp:\\s*:([a-z0-9_]+)/)\n    return m && m[1]\n  })\n  for (const n of names) {\n    if (reg.packages.some((p) => p.name === n.name)) continue\n    const res = await request(`https://hex.pm/api/packages/${n.name}`)\n    if (res.ok && res.data && pointsToOwners(Object.values(res.data.meta.links || {}))) reg.packages.push({ name: n.name, version: res.data.latest_stable_version, description: short(res.data.meta.description), url: res.data.html_url, downloads: res.data.downloads.all, downloadsPeriod: 'all-time' })\n  }\n  reg.discovery.push(`${names.length} mix.exs apps in repos checked`)\n  return finish(reg)\n}\n\n// ====================================================== Anaconda / AUR / Nimble\nasync function collectAnaconda() {\n  const reg = registry('anaconda', 'Anaconda.org (conda)', 'https://anaconda.org/')\n  for (const account of NAMES) {\n    const res = await request(`https://api.anaconda.org/packages/${account}`)\n    const list = res.ok && Array.isArray(res.data) ? res.data : []\n    reg.accounts.push({ account, kind: 'user', url: `https://anaconda.org/${account}`, found: res.ok, packages: list.length })\n    for (const p of list) reg.packages.push({ name: `${account}/${p.name}`, version: p.latest_version, description: short(p.summary), url: `https://anaconda.org/${account}/${p.name}`, downloads: (p.files || []).reduce((a, f) => a + (f.ndownloads || 0), 0), downloadsPeriod: 'all-time' })\n  }\n  return finish(reg)\n}\nasync function collectAur() {\n  const reg = registry('aur', 'Arch User Repository', 'https://aur.archlinux.org/')\n  for (const by of ['maintainer', 'comaintainers', 'submitter']) {\n    const res = await request(`https://aur.archlinux.org/rpc/v5/search/${USER}?by=${by}`)\n    const list = res.ok && res.data ? res.data.results || [] : []\n    reg.accounts.push({ account: `${USER} (${by})`, kind: by, url: `https://aur.archlinux.org/account/${USER}`, found: list.length > 0, packages: list.length })\n    for (const p of list) if (!reg.packages.some((x) => x.name === p.Name)) reg.packages.push({ name: p.Name, version: p.Version, description: short(p.Description), url: `https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/${p.Name}`, downloads: null, downloadsPeriod: null, votes: p.NumVotes })\n  }\n  return finish(reg)\n}\nasync function collectNimble() {\n  const reg = registry('nimble', 'Nimble (Nim)', 'https://nimble.directory/')\n  const res = await request('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nim-lang/packages/master/packages.json')\n  const list = res.ok && Array.isArray(res.data) ? res.data : []\n  for (const p of list) if (pointsToOwners(p.url, p.web)) reg.packages.push({ name: p.name, version: null, description: short(p.description), url: `https://nimble.directory/pkg/${p.name.toLowerCase()}`, repository: p.url, downloads: null, downloadsPeriod: null })\n  reg.accounts.push({ account: 'nim-lang/packages index (matched by repository URL)', kind: 'index', found: res.ok, packages: reg.packages.length })\n  return finish(reg)\n}\n\n// ============================================ Swift Package Index / Homebrew\nasync function collectSwift(manifest) {\n  const reg = registry('swift', 'Swift Package Index', 'https://swiftpackageindex.com/')\n  for (const c of manifest.swift) {\n    const res = await request(`https://swiftpackageindex.com/${c.repo}`, { as: 'text', tries: 3 })\n    if (res.status === 200) reg.packages.push({ name: c.repo, version: null, description: null, url: `https://swiftpackageindex.com/${c.repo}`, repository: `https://github.com/${c.repo}`, downloads: null, downloadsPeriod: null })\n  }\n  reg.accounts.push({ account: 'root Package.swift files in all repositories', kind: 'derived', found: manifest.swift.length > 0, packages: manifest.swift.length })\n  return finish(reg)\n}\nasync function collectHomebrew(manifest) {\n  const reg = registry('homebrew', 'Homebrew taps', 'https://brew.sh/')\n  const taps = repos.filter((r) => /^homebrew-/i.test(r.name))\n  for (const tap of taps) reg.accounts.push({ account: tap.fullName, kind: 'tap', url: tap.url, found: true, packages: manifest.homebrew.filter((f) => f.repo === tap.fullName).length })\n  for (const f of manifest.homebrew) {\n    const [owner, repo] = f.repo.split('/')\n    reg.packages.push({ name: `${owner.toLowerCase()}/${repo.replace(/^homebrew-/i, '')}/${f.name}`, type: f.kind === 'Formula' ? 'formula' : 'cask', version: null, description: null, url: `https://github.com/${f.repo}/blob/HEAD/${f.path}`, downloads: null, downloadsPeriod: 'third-party taps have no public analytics' })\n  }\n  return finish(reg)\n}\n\n// ===================================================================== main\nasync function main() {\n  const started = Date.now()\n  const manifestScan = await discoverManifests()\n  const m = manifestScan.candidates\n  // Registries with strict rate limits run sequentially inside, the rest in parallel.\n  const tasks = [\n    ['npm', () => collectNpm(m)],\n    ['crates', () => collectCrates(m)],\n    ['nuget', () => collectNuget(m)],\n    ['pypi', () => collectPypi(m)],\n    ['dockerhub', collectDocker],\n    ['github-packages', collectGithubPackages],\n bx, ay - by];\nconst scale = ([x, y], k) => [x * k, y * k];\nconst len = ([x, y]) => Math.hypot(x, y) || 1;\nconst unit = (v) => scale(v, 1 / len(v));\nconst dir = (angle) => [Math.cos(angle), Math.sin(angle)];\nconst left = ([x, y]) => [y, -x];\nconst DEG = Math.PI / 180;\n\n// The arrow (target marker) and the bar (source marker) at `end`, oriented by `tangent`.\nfunction arrow(end, tangent) {\n  const back = scale(unit(tangent), -5.5);\n  const a = add(end, rotate(back, 28 * DEG));\n  const b = add(end, rotate(back, -28 * DEG));\n  return `M${pt(a)}L${pt(end)}L${pt(b)}`;\n}\nfunction bar(end, tangent) {\n  const n = scale(left(unit(tangent)), 3.4);\n  return `M${pt(add(end, n))}L${pt(sub(end, n))}`;\n}\nfunction rotate([x, y], a) {\n  return [x * Math.cos(a) - y * Math.sin(a), x * Math.sin(a) + y * Math.cos(a)];\n}\n\n// A curved half from link dot `from` to dot `to`, bent sideways by `bend`.\nfunction half(from, to, bend, marker) {\n  const d = sub(to, from);\n  const u = unit(d);\n  const control = add(add(from, scale(d, 0.5)), scale(left(u), bend * len(d)));\n  const start = add(from, scale(unit(sub(control, from)), DOT_RADIUS + 1.2));\n  const endTangent = unit(sub(to, control));\n  const end = sub(to, scale(endTangent, DOT_RADIUS + 1.6));\n  return `M${pt(start)}Q${pt(control)} ${pt(end)}` + marker(end, endTangent);\n}\n\n// A teardrop petal that leaves dot `at` in direction `angle` and comes back.\nfunction petal(at, angle, reach, spread, marker) {\n  const c1 = add(at, scale(dir(angle + spread), reach));\n  const c2 = add(at, scale(dir(angle - spread), reach));\n  const start = add(at, scale(dir(angle + spread), DOT_RADIUS + 1.2));\n  const end = add(at, scale(dir(angle - spread), DOT_RADIUS + 1.6));\n  return `M${pt(start)}C${pt(c1)} ${pt(c2)} ${pt(end)}` + marker(end, unit(sub(end, c2)));\n}\n\n/**\n * Paths of a configuration given as `[[source, target], …]` (link indices).\n * Returns `{ stroke, dots }`: one SVG path for all strokes and dot centers.\n */\nexport function glyphPaths(links) {\n  const n = links.length;\n  const dots = LAYOUTS[n];\n  if (!dots) throw new RangeError(`Only 1–4 links are supported, got ${n}`);\n  const center = scale(dots.reduce(add, [0, 0]), 1 / n);\n  const reach = n === 1 ? 34 : 24;\n  const parts = links.map(([s, t], i) => {\n    const at = dots[i];\n    // Petals point away from the other links; a lone link opens left and right.\n    const out = n === 1 ? Math.PI : both ? out + 52 * DEG : out;\n    const targetAngle = n === 1 ? 0 : both ? out - 52 * DEG : out;\n    const source = s === i ? petal(at, sourceAngle, reach, 34 * DEG, bar) : half(at, dots[s], 0.16, bar);\n    const target = t === i ? petal(at, targetAngle, reach, 34 * DEG, arrow) : half(at, dots[t], -0.26, arrow);\n    return source + target;\n  });\n  return { stroke: parts.join(''), dots };\n}\n\n/** Standalone SVG markup of a configuration (used for the sprite and the gallery). */\nexport function glyphSymbol(links, id) {\n  const { stroke, dots } = glyphPaths(links);\n  const circles = dots.map(([x, y]) => `<circle cx=\"${x}\" cy=\"${y}\" r=\"${DOT_RADIUS}\"/>`).join('');\n  return (\n    `<symbol id=\"${id}\" viewBox=\"0 0 ${SIZE} ${SIZE}\">` +\n    `<path d=\"${stroke}\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"2.4\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\"/>` +\n    `<g fill=\"currentColor\">${circles}</g></symbol>`\n  );\n}\n\n/** Symbol id of a canonical configuration code such as `\"01 10\"`. */\nexport const glyphId = (code) => `links-${code.split(' ').length}-${code.replace(/ /g, '-')}`;\n"

[**Problem Formulation**](https://github.com/Konard/problem-solving/blob/main/problem-solving/problem-formulation/problem-formulation.md): This step involves fully understanding and defining the problem that needs to be solved. This includes defining the problem in clear, precise terms and breaking it down into smaller, manageable parts. Alongside this understanding, you also formulate failing tests based on the problem's definition. These tests serve as concrete goals that the solution should achieve. The aim of this step is to transform the initial problem into a well-defined set of failing tests that clearly express what a solution to the problem should look like.\n\n2. After making the tests pass, you refine the solution through debugging and refactoring to improve its structure and performance without changing its behavior. This step is iterative and may involve revisiting the problem formulation stage if new information or difficulties arise, or if the tests need to be updated. Finally, documenting the solution for future reference and for others' understanding is an integral part of this step.\n\nNote: On any step of the algorithm it is possible that problem definition will change or is required to be changed for  solution to be possible or efficient. Each push to `main` publishes a complete release automatically; it can also be run manually on `main`. A rerun of the same commit reuses its release, and an interrupted upload resumes the draft before publication. We believe that the concepts discussed here can serve as inspiration across a wide range of scientific disciplines.\n\nOur goal was to create a self-contained text that guides you through each topic in a clear, logical order. The text is intended to be easily understood when read from start to finish.\n\nEvery symbol and formula is explained individually, with concise definitions provided where needed. We’ve also included images to help illustrate key ideas. If you come across anything that isn’t clear, please let us know so we can improve it.\n\n### The links theory\n\nThe links theory is based on the concept of a link.\n\nIn the projection of the links theory into set theory, [a link](https://habr.com/ru/companies/deepfoundation/articles/576398) is defined as an [n-tuple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuple) of references to links, which has its own reference that other links can use to refer to it.\n\n> It is worth noting that the separate notion of a reference is required here solely because [circular definitions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_definition) are not available in set theory. In fact, the links theory can describe itself without needing a distinct term for a reference — in other words, a reference is simply a special case of a link.\n\n#### Duplets\n\nA doublet-link is represented by a duplet (2-tuple or [ordered pair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordered_pair)) of references to links. A doublet-link also has its own reference.\n\n```python\nL = { 1 , 2 }\n\nL × L = {\n  (1, 1),\n  (1, 2),\n  (2, 1),\n  (2, 2),\n}\n```\n\n**Where**:\n\n- $L$ is the set of references (from the English word “Links” as in “References”).\n\nIn this example, the set $L$ contains only $2$ references to links, namely $1$ and $2$. In other words, in a network of links built on such a set of references, there can be only $2$ links.\n\nTo obtain all possible values of a link, [the Cartesian product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartesian_product) of $L$ with itself is used, i.e., $L \\times L$.\n\n![Figure 4](images/figure-4.png)\n\n**Figure 4.** A matrix representing the Cartesian product of the set {1, 2} with itself. Here we see that links with two references to links can have only 4 possible values.\n\n![Figure 5](images/figure-5.png)\n\n**Figure 5.** A table of rows containing all possible variants of link values for a network with two links; these variants are obtained using the Cartesian product of {1, 2} with itself.\n\nThe **doublet-links network** is defined as:\n### The links theory definitions within set theory framework\n\nA **reference to a vector** is a unique identifier or ordinal number, which is associated with a specific vector representing a sequence of references to other vectors.\n\nSet of references to vectors:\n\n> $\\displaystyle \\mathbf{L ⊆ ℕ_0}$\n\nA **vector of references** is a vector consisting of zero or more references to vectors, where the number of references corresponds to the number of elements in the vector.\n\nSet of all vectors of references of length $n ∈ ℕ_0$:\n\n> $\\displaystyle \\mathbf{V_n = L^n}$\n\nThe Cartesian power $L^n$ always produces a vector of length $n$ , since all its components are of the same type $L$.\nIn other words, $L^n$ represents the set of all possible n-element vectors (essentially n‑tuples), in which every element belongs to the set $L$.\n\nAn **association** is an ordered pair consisting of a reference to a vector and a vector of references. This structure serves as a mapping between references and vectors.\n\n> $\\displaystyle \\mathbf{A = L \\times V_n}$\n\nAn **associative network** of vectors of length **n** (or an n-dimensional associative network) is defined by a family of functions $\\{anetv^n\\}$, where each function $anetv^n: L → V_n$ maps a reference $l ∈ L$ to a vector of references of length $n$, belonging to $V_n$, thereby identifying points in an n-dimensional space.\n$n$ in $anetv^n$ indicates that the function returns vectors containing $n$ references. Each n-dimensional associative network thus represents a sequence of points in n-dimensional space.\n\n**Family of functions:**\n\n> $\\displaystyle \\mathbf{∪_f \\{anetv^n | n ∈ ℕ_0\\} ⊆ A}$\n\nHere, the union symbol $∪_f$ denotes the aggregation of all functions in the family $\\{anetv^n\\}$, and the symbol $⊆$ indicates that these ordered pairs — viewed as functional binary relations — are a subset of the set $A$ of all associations.\n\n**Set of duplets (ordered pairs or 2-dimensional vectors) of references:**\n\n> $\\displaystyle \\mathbf{D = L^2}$\n\nThis is the set of all duplets $(L, L)$, i.e., the second Cartesian power of $L$ .\n\n**Associative network of duplets (or a 2-dimensional associative network):**\n\n> $\\displaystyle \\mathbf{anetd: L → L^2}$\n\nEach associative network of duplets thus represents a sequence of points in a two‑dimensional space.\n\nAn empty vector (vector of length zero) is represented by the empty tuple, denoted as $()$ or $∅$.\n\n**Associative network of nested ordered pairs:**\n\n## Conclusion\n\nIn this article, we examined the mathematical foundations of relational algebra and graph theory, and presented the definitions of the links theory in terms of set theory and its projection into type theory. We also defined a set of functions and lemmas necessary for proving the possibility of an equivalent conversion from any vector/sequence into nested doublet-links and back. This means that only one formula is sufficient to represent any possible type of information:\n\n> $\\displaystyle L \\to L^2$\n\nThus, this forms the basis for testing the hypothesis that any other data structure can be represented by doublet-links. In other words, doublet-links are sufficient to represent any tables, graphs, strings, arrays, lists, numbers, sound, images, videos, and much more.\n\nAnother consequence of this proof is that we can represent tape of Turing Machine using only doublet‑links. That means links can be as powerful as a Turing Machine in its storage capacity. Meaning we can use links for all use cases there Turing Machine is used. But there is no need to try to fit data into zeroes and ones, no need to puzzle about that. Because in links the “alphabet” is essentially is unlimited and you can add any number of links, assign to them any meaning you need and link or connect them together in any way you need. Usually it means that your concept, object or thing from the real or abstract world will be mapped 1 to 1 into links or as close to original as possible, which is sometimes not possible with traditional methods.\n\nWe continue to make progress in synchronizing meaning between our three projects and among the people in our associative community. y * Math.sin(a), x * Math.sin(a) + y * Math.cos(a)];\n}\n\n// A curved half from link dot `from` to dot `to`, bent sideways by `bend`.\nfunction half(from, to, bend, marker) {\n  const d = sub(to, from);\n  const u = unit(d);\n  const control = add(add(from, scale(d, 0.5)), scale(left(u), bend * len(d)));\n  const start = add(from, scale(unit(sub(control, from)), DOT_RADIUS + 1.2));\n  const endTangent = unit(sub(to, control));\n  const end = sub(to, scale(endTangent, DOT_RADIUS + 1.6));\n  return `M${pt(start)}Q${pt(control)} ${pt(end)}` + marker(end, endTangent);\n}\n\n// A teardrop petal that leaves dot `at` in direction `angle` and comes back.\nfunction petal(at, angle, reach, spread, marker) {\n  const c1 = add(at, scale(dir(angle + spread), reach));\n  const c2 = add(at, scale(dir(angle -
